explanation: Traverse nodes with their depths, tracking the smallest and largest depths encountered at leaves. Reject once their difference exceeds one.
correctness: The stored extremes are exactly the extrema among visited leaves. The final spread is the required global condition; an excessive partial spread can never decrease when more leaves are visited.
walkthrough: For [4,2,7,1,3,null,9], the leaves are 1, 3 and 9. Each is two edges below the root, so the shallowest and deepest depths are both 2 and their difference is 0. Return true. A long chain would also return true because it has only one leaf.
edgeCases: leaf depths in separate subtrees. This is not per-node AVL height balance.
An empty tree returns true, and a chain of any supported length returns true because its only leaf supplies both depth extremes.
timeComplexity: O(n) time: each of n nodes is pushed and visited at most once, with constant work per visit.
spaceComplexity: O(h) auxiliary space: depth-first pending siblings occupy at most a constant number of entries per tree level; h can be n.
